pairs.question: Plus solito coeunt ad gaudia; dic, amice, quid sit! Romam per omnem cursitant ouantque?
pairs.answer: Festus apostolici nobis redit hic dies triumfi, Pauli atque Petri nobilis cruore.
pairs.derivation: The poem opens with two speakers. The first speaker's entire utterance (lines 3-4) is the question: he observes crowds gathering and explicitly asks 'dic, amice, quid sit' (tell me, friend, what it is). Quoted whole and contiguous; capitalization kept, terminal '!' on the imperative retained and a '?' added to mark the genuine interrogative. The respondent's reply (lines 5-68) is long; the operative answering sentence is its first: 'Festus apostolici nobis redit hic dies triumfi, Pauli atque Petri nobilis cruore.' (ends at the full stop after 'cruore'). Everything after that point (Vnus utrumque dies... and the rest of the topographical/martyrdom elaboration through line 68) is digression beyond the direct answer and is cut. Stripped scaffolding: title line, and trailing 'Prudentius / Christian Latin / The Latin Library / The Classics Page' footer. No section markers or angle-bracket supplements present.
